topology: 1 node x4 H100, NCCL over NVLink, host-API capture only (no NVBit)
why: The suite ran NCCL twice and captured the collective layer neither time. Case 02 sees the verbs underneath an all-reduce, case 05 sees GPU accesses that land in NCCL's internal channel buffers and attribute to nothing. Which collective ran, over which buffers, between which peers, was in no capture. This case is that layer, and it is the only NCCL point-to-point in the suite.
cost_note: Seconds, not minutes. No NVBit, one node, small messages — the provider hooks host API calls and touches no CUDA context. Case 05's 481 s is fixed NVBit module-processing cost and is unrelated.
workload_note: `mpirun -np 4 --map-by ppr:4:node ... nccl_collectives 65536 2`. Unlike cases 02 and 05, the derived counts here ARE assertable from the command line: this provider records the calls the APPLICATION made, and NCCL's channel/protocol choices cannot change how many times the application called ncclAllReduce. That is the difference between the operation layer and the wire — 02's workload_note explains why the same arithmetic is meaningless there.
not_covered: nccl_window and nccl_dev_comm stay empty here: they are the device-initiated path (ncclCommWindowRegister / ncclDevCommCreate), which needs a kernel using the NCCL device API. That is the GPU-initiated case, and it is separate work. The two tables are absent rather than empty in this capture, which is the honest state — nothing in this workload opens those doors.
